001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.jfr;
002
003import java.io.IOException;
004import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
005import java.net.URI;
006import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
007import java.nio.file.Path;
008
009import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
010
011import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogConfig;
012import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEncoder;
013import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEvent;
014import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEncoder.BufferHints;
015import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogFormatter;
016import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogFormatter.ThrowableFormatter;
017import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogOutput;
018import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogOutput.WriteMethod;
019
020import jdk.jfr.Recording;
021
022/**
023 * A {@link LogOutput} that commits each log event as a JFR event (see
024 * {@link RainbowGumLogEvent}) instead of writing anywhere.
025 * <p>
026 * The output prefers {@link WriteMethod#STRING}, so formatter-backed encoders hand the
027 * formatted message directly to {@link #write(LogEvent, String)} without first turning it
028 * into bytes:
029 *
030 * <pre>{@code
031 * logging.appender.myappender.output=jfr:///
032 * }</pre>
033 *
034 * Per-event-type enablement, thresholds, and stack trace capture are controlled the same
035 * way as any other JFR event, e.g. with {@code -XX:StartFlightRecording} or a
036 * {@code .jfc} settings file - not through Rainbow Gum properties. If a Flight Recorder
037 * session that enables the relevant event type is not running, {@link #write} does
038 * (cheaply) nothing.
039 * <p>
040 * If the configured URI has a real path (anything past the root {@code /}), this output
041 * instead starts and owns its own {@link Recording} writing directly to that file for as
042 * long as the output is open, with every event type unconditionally enabled:
043 *
044 * <pre>{@code
045 * logging.appender.myappender.output=jfr:///var/log/myapp.jfr
046 * }</pre>
047 *
048 * In this mode JFR's own per-event enablement/threshold filtering is bypassed entirely -
049 * whether an event is captured is decided solely by Rainbow Gum's normal level resolver
050 * (the same one that already decides whether {@link #write} is called at all), not by JFR
051 * settings.
052 * <p>
053 * This output also implements {@link LogOutput.ProvidesEncoder}, supplying (as an
054 * overridable default, see {@link LogOutput.ProvidesEncoder.Policy#DEFAULT}) an encoder
055 * that renders the message followed by any key values, e.g. {@code some message -
056 * {key=value}} - no timestamp/level/logger prefix, since the JFR event already carries
057 * those as separate fields - so leaving {@code encoder} unset when {@code output=jfr:///}
058 * picks this up automatically instead of the default TTLL encoder formatting a whole line
059 * only to throw most of it away.
060 */
061public final class JfrLogOutput implements LogOutput, LogOutput.ProvidesEncoder {
062
063        /**
064         * JFR output URI scheme.
065         */
066        public static final String JFR_SCHEME = "jfr";
067
068        private static final URI JFR_URI = URI.create(JFR_SCHEME + ":///");
069
070        /**
071         * Renders the message followed by any key values, e.g. {@code some message -
072         * {key=value}}. Shared with {@link JfrAlertListener}, which renders alerts the same
073         * way.
074         */
075        static final LogFormatter MESSAGE_FORMATTER = LogFormatter.builder()
076                .message()
077                .text(" - {")
078                .keyValues()
079                .text("}")
080                .build();
081
082        private final URI uri;
083
084        private final @Nullable Path destination;
085
086        private volatile @Nullable Recording recording;
087
088        /**
089         * Creates a JFR output that emits events only for whatever externally started Flight
090         * Recorder session (if any) is currently running, without managing a recording of its
091         * own.
092         */
093        public JfrLogOutput() {
094                this(JFR_URI, null);
095        }
096
097        /**
098         * Creates a JFR output.
099         * @param uri the output's own configured URI, returned as-is by {@link #uri()}.
100         * @param destination if not null, a file this output starts and owns its own
101         * {@link Recording} against for as long as the output is open (see {@link #start},
102         * {@link #close}); if null, events are only captured by whatever externally started
103         * recording (if any) is already running.
104         */
105        public JfrLogOutput(URI uri, @Nullable Path destination) {
106                this.uri = uri;
107                this.destination = destination;
108        }
109
110        /**
111         * Extracts a recording destination file from a configured output URI, if any. The
112         * default {@code jfr:///} URI has path {@code "/"} (root, no real path segment),
113         * which must not be mistaken for a configured destination file.
114         * @param uri configured output URI.
115         * @return destination file, or null if {@code uri} has no real path.
116         */
117        static @Nullable Path destinationOrNull(URI uri) {
118                String path = uri.getPath();
119                if (path == null || path.length() <= 1) {
120                        return null;
121                }
122                return Path.of(path);
123        }
124
125        @Override
126        public URI uri() {
127                return uri;
128        }
129
130        @Override
131        public void start(LogConfig config) {
132                var path = destination;
133                if (path == null) {
134                        return;
135                }
136                var r = new Recording();
137                r.enable(RainbowGumLogEvent.TraceEvent.class);
138                r.enable(RainbowGumLogEvent.DebugEvent.class);
139                r.enable(RainbowGumLogEvent.InfoEvent.class);
140                r.enable(RainbowGumLogEvent.WarnEvent.class);
141                r.enable(RainbowGumLogEvent.ErrorEvent.class);
142                try {
143                        r.setDestination(path);
144                }
145                catch (IOException e) {
146                        r.close();
147                        throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
148                }
149                r.start();
150                this.recording = r;
151        }
152
153        @Override
154        public OutputType type() {
155                return OutputType.MEMORY;
156        }
157
158        @Override
159        public BufferHints bufferHints() {
160                return WriteMethod.STRING;
161        }
162
163        @Override
164        public LogEncoder encoder(String name, LogConfig config) {
165                return LogEncoder.of(MESSAGE_FORMATTER).provide(name, config);
166        }
167
168        @Override
169        public void write(LogEvent event, String s) {
170                var jfrEvent = RainbowGumLogEvent.of(event.level());
171                if (jfrEvent == null || !jfrEvent.isEnabled()) {
172                        return;
173                }
174                jfrEvent.message = s;
175                jfrEvent.logger = event.loggerName();
176                var t = event.throwableOrNull();
177                if (t != null) {
178                        var stackTrace = new StringBuilder();
179                        ThrowableFormatter.appendThrowable(stackTrace, t);
180                        jfrEvent.throwable = stackTrace.toString();
181                }
182                jfrEvent.commit();
183        }
184
185        @Override
186        public void write(LogEvent event, byte[] bytes, int off, int len, ContentType contentType) {
187                var charset = contentType.charsetOrNull();
188                if (charset == null) {
189                        charset = StandardCharsets.UTF_8;
190                }
191                write(event, new String(bytes, off, len, charset));
192        }
193
194        @Override
195        public void flush() {
196        }
197
198        @Override
199        public void close() {
200                var r = recording;
201                if (r != null) {
202                        r.close();
203                }
204        }
205
206}
